behavior: An unauthenticated Bitwarden session is reported, with severity keyed to whether the registry actually holds backend: bw entries
A stale lastSync warns before the refresh token dies, while bw status still reports the vault as locked
With a session available, reachability is proven by an authenticated round-trip against the server, not by PATH presence
Unusable or unreadable inputs (bad JSON, unknown status, never synced, unreadable registry, future-dated sync) degrade to advisory and never claim verified reach
The severity producer counts only backend: bw entries, reads the checkout registry rather than the deployed mirror, and errors instead of reporting a silent zero when it cannot read

Network-bound bw subprocesses are killed at their deadline rather than hanging the diagnostic (and, through it, setup-linux.sh), and the two streams stay separate so CLI chatter on stderr cannot defeat a stdout parse
bw's own stderr diagnostics do not defeat the status parse: all three tiers still evaluate on a machine where bw has never run before
A sync failure on an unlocked vault follows exposure like every other tier — advisory while nothing resolves through Bitwarden, a failure once something does
The check is wired into the product: a full doctor run emits the Bitwarden reach section, so dropping its registration from Run() fails CI
